Consult ipc.js if anything below looks stale.

docs.title: System architecture
docs.text:
┌─────────────────┐   TCP :55544   ┌─────────────┐   GlobalVars   ┌──────────────┐
│ bridge_ctl.py   │ ◄────────────► │ bridge.js   │ ──────────────►│   main.js    │
│ MCP server "mc" │                │ (Service)   │                │ (Container)  │
└─────────────────┘                └─────────────┘                └──────┬───────┘
                                                                         │
                                                               eval(code)│
                                                                         ▼
                                                                ┌──────────────┐
                                                                │   worker.js  │
                                                                │ (the bundle) │
                                                                └──────────────┘
  • bridge.js — thin TCP gateway Service (default 127.0.0.1:55544, newline-framed JSON). Polls a ServerSocketChannel each tick; no logic — it queues each request line into GlobalVars and relays the correlated response back. Override the bind host via the mc_bridge_host GlobalVar (or the port via mc_bridge_port / bridge_port.txt).
  • main.js — always-on Container Service and stable utility/API container. Owns safeEval, the ServiceManager lifecycle, the ext-plugin registry, and bridge command dispatch, and publishes the render-thread-pinned world reads the worker can't do itself.
  • worker.js — managed Service that evals the built bundle (dist/__gerda_bot.bundle.js, which assigns globalThis.Module) and drives it tick-by-tick, writing a heartbeat.

The three services are isolated eval scopes with no shared module system, so each eval-includes ipc.js and reads the global it publishes (globalThis.__MC_IPC).

docs.title: Bridge → main.js (TCP JSON, \n-framed)
docs.text:
Request { id, type, ...params }, response { ok, type, id, ...data }:

{"type": "<cmd>", "id": 42, "<field>": "..."}
{"ok": true, "type": "<cmd>", "id": 42, "<data>": "..."}

id is the one correlation id that genuinely crosses script contexts (bridge → main → worker); the response carries the same id back.

The command reference is describe. The live command set is larger than the table below and self-describing: the describe bridge command returns every command with its params, merged from main.js HANDLERS, the ext.js plugins and the worker bundle's own commands. Ask for it with ./gerda ctl send describe, or read the mc://api resource of the mc MCP server (the same manifest).

Core container endpoints:

Type Payload fields Description describe — The command manifest: every command and its params status — Container status, module state, service status services — List all registered services and running status get_state — Full state snapshot (pos, health, phase, target, tool, inventory summary) start name? Start managed service (default: worker) stop — Stop managed service or unload module halt — Hard stop (SIGKILL equivalent). It stops the worker synchronously on main's tick, so on a stuck worker it deaf-locks the whole bridge: use reload_worker (./gerda reload-worker) instead, see FLEET_PLAYBOOK § 2.1 reload_worker name?, delay? Off-thread worker reload (halt + start as one command); safe on a stuck worker pause / resume — Passthrough to worker (via GlobalVars) goto x, y, z Passthrough to worker scan radius? Read-only: exposed ores + player state inventory — Read-only: hotbar + main inventory + fullness eval code Evaluate JS in the main.js sandbox (safeEval — World/Player only, no Java) jeval code Privileged escape hatch — full jsMacros/Java scope, loopback only load code Load JS as a passive module (loadModule)

docs.title: main.js ↔ worker.js (GlobalVars)
docs.text: Key Type Direction Purpose mc_worker_cmd string (JSON) main → worker Command payload mc_worker_cmd_flag int (unixtime) main → worker Command freshness flag mc_worker_alive int (tick count) worker → main Heartbeat, incremented at the start of every worker tick body. It does not change while a body blocks; the movement-key dead-man in main.js reads it (see Tick pacing) mc_worker_alive_ts int (unixtime) worker → main Heartbeat wall-clock mc_worker_status string worker → main Worker status line: running · paused · fatal (tick fatal, worker halted) · load_failed (no module: the bundle was missing, threw while loading, or exported no Module) · stopped mc_worker_last_cmd string worker → main Last handled command mc_worker_resp string (JSON) worker → main Ack {id,ok,type,result} (correlated by id) mc_worker_cmds string (JSON) worker → main Bundle's self-described command manifest mc_worker_build string (JSON) worker → main Bundle build stamp {rev,time} mc_worker_fatal string (JSON) worker → main {owner,phase,tick,error,time}: a CoreFatalError from a tick (→ halt), or a bundle load failure (owner:"worker", phase:"loadBundle", plus path). Shown as worker.fatal in get_state and diag; a successful load clears it mc_want_sprint string ("1"/"0") worker → main Desired sprint flag; main applies it on the main thread (setSprinting off-thread races the render FOV read → CME crash) mc_worker_tick_pace string (JSON) worker → main Tick pacing stats {lastMs,maxMs,slow,missed}: slow = ticks that ran longer than 50 ms, missed = game ticks dropped while they ran, maxMs = the longest tick so far. Written at the first tick, then only when slow grows, so lastMs is the duration of the most recent slow tick, not of the latest tick. Shown as worker.tickPace in get_state and diag

docs.title: Tick pacing
docs.text:
jsMacros 1.9 starts a new thread for every JsMacros.on("Tick", …) listener on every game tick. The thread then waits for the script's one GraalJS context. If one tick body runs for a long time, the threads pile up behind it: on a CPU-starved client a 4-minute worker tick left 4538 waiting threads, and the client died with unable to create native thread.

So bridge.js, main.js and worker.js tick through IPC.paceTick (harness/ipc.js). It arms one JsMacros.once("Tick", …) listener and arms the next one only when the body returns. While a body runs, no Tick listener exists and jsMacros starts no thread. The game ticks of that time are dropped, not queued. diag.main.tickPace and worker.tickPace count them.

Because the worker runs no new body while one runs, mc_worker_alive stops for as long as a worker tick blocks. main.js uses this as a movement-key dead-man: when the value does not change for DEADMAN_STALE_TICKS (10) main ticks, main.js releases the movement, jump, sprint and sneak keys once for that stall (docs/SAFETY.md). Each stall also writes a DEADMAN record to the journal (miner.ndjson), so get_logs shows it. The record's tick is the worker heartbeat (mc_worker_alive, the worker's tick count, as on every other record); main's own count is fields.mainTick. diag reports the dead-man as main.deadman:

Field Meaning staleTicks The threshold, DEADMAN_STALE_TICKS stalls Worker stalls since main.js started. Each one released the keys, but main.js cannot see which keys the worker held, so a stall with no key down (a long SCAN tick) counts too. It is not a count of prevented falls. lastStallTick The main tick of the last release (-1 = never) stalledTicks Main ticks since mc_worker_alive last changed tripped The current stall already released the keys

docs.title: bridge.js ↔ main.js (GlobalVars)
docs.text: Key Type Purpose mc_bridge_cmd_count int Monotonic counter for commands from the bridge mc_bridge_seq int Bridge sequence cursor mc_bridge_cmd_<N> string (JSON) Queued request line N mc_bridge_resp_<id> string (JSON) Response line for command id mc_bridge_alive int Container heartbeat mc_bridge_host / mc_bridge_port string / int Runtime bind host / port override (else bridge_port.txt / 55544)

docs.title: main.js boot, heartbeat & event ring
docs.text: main.js also publishes its own boot/heartbeat keys — mc_main_alive, mc_main_build ({rev,time}), and mc_main_srg_ok + mc_main_srg_missing (the loud SRG-resolution boot diagnosis) — plus a bounded pull event ring (mc_events_seq / _head / _size / _slot_<i>, capacity 256) that backs the poll_events / get_logs endpoints.

docs.title: Shared world model (main → worker)
docs.text:
Some reads are pinned to main.js's thread and deadlock or crash if the worker attempts them, so main.js publishes them each tick and the worker mirrors them for the bundle: mc_world_sig ("<wid>|<dim>", for world.signature()), mc_items / mc_mobs / mc_peers / mc_frames (nearby-entity JSON snapshots), mc_assignment (fleet region), and the mc_world.json file store.

GlobalVars is a thread-safe ConcurrentHashMap but rejects guest (JS) objects — everything above the wire is primitives / Strings / JSON by necessity, not just convention.

docs.title: Build & deploy
docs.text:
The bundle is built by tsup (just build → dist/__gerda_bot.bundle.js, IIFE/es2020) and deployed with sync.py, which is deploy-only — it copies the built bundle plus the harness/ service files into each game instance.

just build                                  # tsup → dist/__gerda_bot.bundle.js
just sync                                   # build + deploy to every instance
python3 scripts/ops/bridge_ctl.py status    # or: ./gerda ctl status

Required jsMacros services: main.js and bridge.js, registered once in the jsMacros Services screen (SETUP.md, Quickstart step 6). main.js starts and manages worker.js.

docs.title: Missions
docs.text:
The reference for the bot's mission system. A mission is a pluggable goal state-machine (src/shared/kernel/mission.ts). The kernel loads ALL missions into a registry and runs exactly one at a time, switchable at runtime with mission_start and no reload. A mission brings its own initialPhase, edges, per-phase handlers, params, an optional completion check (isDone) and result (outputs), plus movementPhases and onAbort. Reflexes (see SAFETY.md § Reaction tier) and the global handlers (RECOVER, lifecycle) live in the kernel, mission-agnostic, and run under every mission.

Drive missions over the bridge:

  • mission_start {name, params?} — activate a mission by name (no reload).
  • mission_abort — stop the active mission → IDLE.
  • mission_status — log the active mission + phase.
  • missions — log the registered mission names (each self-describes its params).

Coordinates in the examples below are placeholders: use your own chest's, furnace's or destination's coordinates.

A plan (the orchestrator, src/bot/orchestrator/) chains missions into an ordered sequence; a completed mission's outputs can feed the next step's params — see Mission chaining below.

Writing a new mission: read docs/EXTENDING.md § Writing a mission (the two authoring styles, the facade contract, the SRG workflow). The worked template is examples/advanced/patrol-mission.ts — a complete, small mission that exercises every part of the contract.

docs.title: Contract notes that apply to all missions
docs.text:
• Two authoring styles. missionFromCaps(name, caps, opts) composes a mission from capability modules (their handlers/guards/edges merged) — used by mine, chop, drill. Caveat: the composed capability inits do NOT receive mission_start params, so a composed mission's params (e.g. count, ore) are read in the mission-level init and pushed into shared slices before the caps tick. All other missions are hand-written Mission objects (so their init(ctx, params) sees params).
  • Params are self-described (a ParamSpec list: name/type/required/desc). Types are string | int | float | bool. Parsing is normalized via _params.ts (parseIdList, intParam, intParamOr, toSet).
  • required is a description, not an enforced gate here. The coordinate missions (goto/fetch/stash/interact) parse x/y/z with the strict intParam; a missing/invalid coordinate leaves the target null and the first tick finishes as a graceful no-op (*_GAVE_UP/"no target"), it does not ERROR. smelt's output is declared required but init defaults it to "".
  • The shared GOTO leg (walkTo, _goto-leg.ts). Every "walk to a fixed stand, then arrive / time-out / give-up-when-blocked" phase uses this one driver (goto, fetch, stash, prospect, storage, loot-run, search). It owns the arrival radius (cfg.nav.gotoArrivalDist), the phase timeout (cfg.nav.gotoTimeoutTicks), the greedy step, and the arrived | blocked_no_path verdict; the caller supplies the arrive/blocked/timeout callbacks. It is a column (Y-free), best-effort approach: a block ends the leg, no ore-style dig escalation. interact, hunt, follow use bespoke legs (moving targets / interact-anyway-when-in-reach).
  • movementPhases tells the reflex layer "movement here is bot-driven", so the stuck/human-input reflexes don't read greedy's own key.forward as a human takeover.
  • Tunables live in src/shared/config/schema.ts — every default below that reads cfg.* resolves there.

docs.title: Registered missions
docs.text:
Only the 15 missions registered in src/bot/entry/worker-bundle.ts are documented. src/bot/missions/harvest/ is not a mission: it holds the shared ore and wood harvest profiles that mine, chop and drill import.

Mission What it does Key params mine Surface-mine ore: scan → walk → break + vein-follow, auto dump when full count drill Dig a shaft to a cached prospector vein and strip-mine its volume ore chop Fell trees: the mine loop with a wood harvest profile count fetch Walk to a chest and withdraw items x,y,z,items stash Walk to a chest and deposit whitelisted items (fail-loud) x,y,z,items storage Route items into the base storage network (drawers + chests) items loot-run Sweep registered containers and take their contents items,near search Serpentine grid survey, recording containers to the world model cols,rows,step smelt Drive a furnace/machine: load, wait, collect (region-agnostic) output,input,fuel craft Craft a recipe chain via manual grid placement chain,want goto Walk to a fixed x/y/z, best-effort x,y,z prospect Walk to the nearest cached vein of an ore group ore hunt Seek → chase → melee huntable mobs count,targets follow Trail a peer at a follow-gap (persistent) target,gap interact Right-click a held item onto a block or item-frame entity x,y,z,item,profile

docs.title: mine
docs.text:
Surface-mining loop (missionFromCaps, composing inventory, loot, scan, navigation, mine, homeReturn, storage). Scans for the configured ore, greedy-walks to a reachable side-stand, breaks it and drains the local vein/layer cluster, sheds junk and diverts HOME→DUMP→RETURN when the bag fills. Ore selection is cfg-driven (oreProfile(ctx.cfg)) — there is no ore param.

name type required default desc count int no 0 (unlimited) stop after N ore broken (0/omit = mine until aborted/exhausted)

Phases: SCAN → GOTO → MINE (with LOOT diverts and HOME → DUMP → RETURN on a full bag), the full TRANSITIONS table. movementPhases: {GOTO, HOME, RETURN, LOOT}. An unreachable ore is skipped, not fatal (onBlocked: "skip"): a blocked greedy verdict, or a GOTO that advances no cell along its planned route for cfg.nav.gotoStallTicks (NAV_GOTO_STALL — a detour that leads away first still advances), caches the target and returns to SCAN. chop shares both.

Completion: isDone = count > 0 && (broken ≥ count || exhausted) — only a bounded batch self-completes; an unlimited run never does (it parks at PAUSED when exhausted). Outputs: { mined, origin, exhausted }.

Notable: onBlocked = "skip" — when a dense patch walls off the walkable side-stand, it caches that ore and re-scans for a reachable one instead of ERRORing the run (contrast drill, which digs to it).

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "mine", "params": {"count": 64}}'

docs.title: drill
docs.text:
Dig to a prospected vein and strip-mine it (missionFromCaps, composing navigation, descend, digTo, excavate, mine, scan). The HV prospector (ext.js prospect, run first) caches veins as surface X/Z in mc_world.json; this mission reads the nearest cached vein of the requested ore group, walks to its X/Z, digs a 1-wide shaft straight down (DESCEND, real hammer) until the shaft exposes the ore, strip-mines the vein VOLUME (EXCAVATE), and hands each exposed clump to MINE's vein-follow.

name type required default desc ore string no via drillProfile(cfg, …) ore group, e.g. iron/gold

Phases: GOTO → DESCEND → EXCAVATE ⇄ MINE, with DIG_TO and SCAN. movementPhases: {GOTO, DIG_TO, EXCAVATE, DESCEND} (DESCEND's step-1 walk-onto-marker is a sustained bot-driven walk).

Completion: no isDone override — the mission never self-completes; it ends via the graceful PAUSE at the end of the corridor plan, or abort. Outputs: { mined, vein }.

Notable: onBlocked = "dig" — when greedy can't WALK to the next ore (offset/above in solid rock), it mines a staircase/tunnel to it (DIG_TO) rather than skipping. No cached vein → a graceful PAUSE + DRILL_NEEDS_PROSPECT alert (recoverable by recharge + prospect + resume), not a hard ERROR. warnIfMissingTool(pickaxe, ore) warns loudly (not blocking) if the bag can't harvest that ore's tier.

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "drill", "params": {"ore": "iron"}}'

docs.title: chop
docs.text:
Fell trees — the same loop as mine (missionFromCaps composing a bagWatch, loot, scan, navigation, mine) with the WOOD harvest profile. Scans for logs, walks, breaks, and diverts to LOOT so felled logs (which land 2-3 blocks away, outside vanilla pickup range) are actually collected.

name type required default desc count int no 0 (until none) stop after N logs (0/omit = until none)

Phases: SCAN → GOTO → MINE with LOOT. movementPhases: {GOTO, LOOT}.

Completion: isDone = count > 0 && (broken ≥ count || exhausted). It deliberately also completes on exhausted even with a count goal, so a bot in a treeless area (e.g. one that respawned somewhere treeless) doesn't spin CHOP_SCAN_EXHAUSTED forever. Outputs: { logs, exhausted }. onAbort: release keys + nav stop.

Notable: onBlocked = "skip" — canopy logs past a safe-fall hazard veto are skipped, not walled on (a forest has many trees). bagWatch ends a full-bag run gracefully via the shared exhausted path. warnIfMissingTool(axe) (warn-only — felling without an axe works, just slowly).

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "chop", "params": {"count": 16}}'

docs.title: fetch
docs.text:
Walk to a chest and withdraw items. Hand-written to demonstrate a mission authored directly (shares nothing with mine except the kernel/reflex/GOTO layer).

name type required default desc x int yes — chest X y int yes — chest Y z int yes — chest Z items string no omit = all ids to withdraw — JSON array ["minecraft:coal"] or CSV; omit → withdraw all

Phases: GOTO → RESTOCK → IDLE (RESTOCK is an internal OPEN → WITHDRAW sub-step). movementPhases: {GOTO}.

Completion: isDone after a successful withdraw, immediately if there's no target, or if GOTO gives up (no self-heal — one target). Outputs: none. onAbort: close screen + nav stop.

Notable: RESTOCK must useOnBlock to open the chest GUI before reading its slots — rt.inv.open() reflects only the currently-open screen. stepOpen is fail-loud: a chest GUI that doesn't open within cfg.containerOpenGraceTicks → ERROR, never a silent empty withdraw.

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "fetch", "params": {"x": 100, "y": 64, "z": 200, "items": ["minecraft:coal"]}}'

docs.title: stash
docs.text:
Walk to a single chest and deposit whitelisted items. The mirror of fetch for the deposit direction; fail-loud on a rejected deposit.

name type required default desc x int yes — chest X y int yes — chest Y z int yes — chest Z items string yes — ids to deposit — JSON array ["minecraft:raw_iron"] or CSV

Phases: GOTO → STASH → IDLE (STASH is an internal OPEN → DEPOSIT → DONE). movementPhases: {GOTO}.

Completion: isDone after deposit, or immediately if there's no chest target / GOTO gives up. Outputs: { deposited }. onAbort: close screen + nav stop.

Notable: region-agnostic — shift-clicks (vanilla quick) carry slots whose id is on the whitelist, highest slot first (so a compacting container doesn't shift indices), and verifies the bag's count actually dropped. A silent quick() failure → STASH_BLOCKED + hard ERROR ("chest full or shift-click rejected"). stepOpen timeout → ERROR too.

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "stash", "params": {"x": 100, "y": 64, "z": 200, "items": ["minecraft:raw_iron", "minecraft:raw_copper"]}}'

docs.title: storage
docs.text:
Route items into the base storage network (kernel-native). Plans the deposit across the registered storages, walks between them, and deposits by kind: drawers (stand + aim slot quadrant + useOnBlock per stack) vs chests (open GUI + shift-click auto-route).

name type required default desc items string yes — ids to deposit into the network — JSON array ["minecraft:raw_iron"] or CSV

Phases: GOTO ⇄ STORE (walk to each visit's stand, deposit, advance to the next). movementPhases: {GOTO}.

Completion: isDone once all planned visits are exhausted (or immediately: nothing to deposit, empty registry). Outputs: { deposited, unplaced } (unplaced = ids the planner couldn't route). onAbort: close screen + nav stop.

Notable: the client-sync boundary — drawers are read LIVE (rt.storage.read, contents replicate client-side); chests/barrels are server-only headless, so they route from the recorded snapshot in the registry and a chest visit writes back the updated snapshot (the "chest with memory", capped at 27 slots). Best-effort skip, not ERROR: an unreachable stand, a drawer slot rejecting an item after the grace window (STORAGE_DRAWER_BLOCKED), or a chest GUI that won't open (STORAGE_CHEST_NO_GUI) all skip and keep the item. The drawer AIM→USE is a deliberate 2-tick gap so the new rotation flushes to the server before its use-raycast.

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "storage", "params": {"items": ["minecraft:iron_ingot", "minecraft:copper_ingot"]}}'

docs.title: loot-run
docs.text:
Sweep registered containers and take their contents. Greedy nearest-neighbour walk over the container visit list, opening each and quick-taking (whitelisted or all).

name type required default desc items string no omit = all only take these ids — JSON array or CSV; omit = take everything near int no null (all) only loot containers within this many blocks of the start breakBlocked bool no false mine off a solid block capping a chest instead of skipping it (leaves a hole; opt-in)

Phases: GOTO ⇄ RANSACK (RANSACK is OPEN → TAKE → CLOSE). movementPhases: {GOTO}.

Completion: isDone after the last visit (or immediately if no candidate containers). Outputs: { taken, containers }. onAbort: close screen + nav stop.

Notable: never ERRORs — an unreachable container, a chest that won't open, or a full inventory all log and advance. Because the GUI is opened (client-synced), the recorded/looted snapshot written back to mc_world.json is exact; looted means the chest is truly empty (so a whitelist run doesn't permanently hide a chest holding other items). Drawers are excluded from LOOTABLE_KINDS (they're the deposit target, not loot). A chest capped by a solid block is skipped (LOOT_BLOCKED) unless breakBlocked mines the cap.

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "loot-run", "params": {"near": 64}}'

docs.title: search
docs.text:
Serpentine (boustrophedon) grid survey that scans a cuboid at each stop and records any containers found into the world model — feeds loot-run/storage.

name type required default desc cols int no cfg.search.cols grid columns rows int no cfg.search.rows grid rows step int no cfg.search.gridStep blocks between stops radius int no cfg.search.scanRadius scan radius per stop height int no cfg.search.scanHeight ± vertical scan reach x int no bot X grid origin X z int no bot Z grid origin Z lanes int no 1 split columns across N bots lane int no 0 this bot's lane index [0..lanes-1]

Phases: GOTO ⇄ SCAN (walk to the next stop, voxel-scan spread over ticks, advance). movementPhases: {GOTO}.

Completion: isDone when all grid points are visited/skipped (or the grid is empty). Outputs: { found, stops }. onAbort: nav stop.

Notable: even rows walk left→right, odd rows reverse — one continuous path. Multi-bot lane striping keeps only columns where c % lanes === lane. The scan is budgeted (cfg.search.scanPerTick) so it never storms getBlock in one tick. Never ERRORs — an unreachable stop is logged and skipped (like loot-run).

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "search", "params": {"cols": 8, "rows": 8, "step": 16}}'

docs.title: smelt
docs.text:
Drive a furnace (or any single-input→single-output machine that honours shift-click) — load, wait, collect. Region-agnostic: it never hardcodes slot/region names; loading rides vanilla shift-click auto-routing and progress is read by matching the output item id in the open screen's non-player slots.

name type required default desc mode string no full full (load+wait+collect) | load (load & leave) | collect (drain ready output) input string no "" raw item id to smelt; required for full/load, unused for collect output string yes* "" expected smelted id (e.g. minecraft:iron_ingot) fuel string no null fuel item id (omit for electric/pre-fueled) count int no 0 collect ≥ this many output (0 = the loaded batch) x int no use open screen furnace block X y int no use open screen furnace block Y z int no use open screen furnace block Z

* output is declared required but init defaults it to "" — no hard abort.

Phases: one kernel SMELT state driving an internal OPEN → LOAD → WAIT → COLLECT → DONE step machine (with mode shortcuts). Stationary — no movementPhases.

Completion: isDone when the step machine reaches DONE. Outputs: { smelted, collected }. onAbort: close screen + release keys.

Notable: the three modes exist for the sustain loop — a furnace cooks server-side in a loaded chunk whether or not the bot waits, so load shifts ore+fuel in and returns immediately (the bot goes mining) and collect comes back to drain. Verify-convention on LOAD (input must leave the bag, else SMELT_LOAD_BLOCKED → ERROR) and COLLECT (re-read the output diff). Asymmetric GUI-lost handling: lost screen in OPEN/LOAD/WAIT → ERROR, in COLLECT → best-effort finish. Live-verified on a vanilla furnace only — GTCEu machine GUIs (macerator/EBF) are UNVERIFIED.

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "smelt", "params": {"mode": "full", "input": "gtceu:raw_iron", "output": "minecraft:iron_ingot", "fuel": "minecraft:coal", "x": 102, "y": 64, "z": 200}}'

docs.title: craft
docs.text:
Craft a recipe chain by manual grid placement (the Monifactory recipe-book API is dead — each chain step carries its grid layout and the server computes the result). Optionally places a crafting table for 3×3 steps.

name type required default desc chain string no cfg.craft.defaultChain JSON [{grid:(id\|null)[], times}] (default → chest from oak logs) table bool no true place a table for the final step want string no null conditional restock: target item id — skip (no-op) if ≥min already carried or materials short min int no 1 want-mode threshold: craft only when carrying fewer than this many want

Phases: one kernel CRAFT state driving an internal CLOSE → PRE → PLACE_TABLE → OPEN_TABLE → FINAL → DONE step machine. Stationary — no movementPhases.

Completion: isDone when the step machine reaches DONE. Outputs: { crafted, tablePos }. onAbort: clear grid (returns items) + close screen + release keys.

Notable: always enters via CLOSE (a prior aborted craft can leave a 3×3 table screen open, corrupting a 2×2 recipe). Place→wait-a-tick→take is split because craft_out fills the tick after placement. Placement and table-open are effect-verified (a "placed" interaction can aim into the ground). Reuses an existing adjacent table before consuming one. The want/min conditional-restock path is deliberately skip-safe (an unattended loop must never stall/ERROR on it) — no-ops to DONE when already stocked or materials short; a plain craft without want still fails loud on a bad recipe.

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "craft", "params": {"want": "minecraft:chest", "min": 1}}'

docs.title: goto
docs.text:
Walk to a fixed x/y/z, best-effort — the standalone form of fetch's GOTO leg with nothing after it (a plan chains it as "walk to the furnace bank" / "return to base").

name type required default desc x int yes — destination X y int yes — destination Y z int yes — destination Z

Phases: GOTO → IDLE. movementPhases: {GOTO}.

Completion: isDone once walkTo resolves (arrive / timeout / blocked). Outputs: { arrived } (true only on GOTO_ARRIVED; false on any give-up). onAbort: nav stop.

Notable: column (Y-free) approach, best-effort — a block ends the trip (no ore-style dig escalation). A missing target finishes the same tick (GOTO_GAVE_UP, arrived:false).

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "goto", "params": {"x": 100, "y": 64, "z": 200}}'

docs.title: prospect
docs.text:
Walk to the nearest un-mined cached vein of an ore group — the goto mission with a dynamically-resolved target. Makes the sustain loop's "shaft" dynamic: reads the HV prospector's vein cache and heads for the closest one.

name type required default desc ore string no cfg.sustain.oreKind vein kind to seek (a PROSPECT_ORE_GROUPS key)

Phases: GOTO → IDLE. movementPhases: {GOTO}.

Completion: isDone the tick it arrives, times out, is blocked, or the cache is empty. Outputs: { found, arrived, target }. onAbort: nav stop.

Notable: an empty cache → PROSPECT_EMPTY + finish (found:false), so a plan can branch (pause for a human to run the ext.js prospect scan) rather than stalling. Reads the world-scoped model off disk to pick the nearest non-depleted vein.

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "prospect", "params": {"ore": "iron"}}'

docs.title: hunt
docs.text:
Seek → chase → melee huntable mobs. Picks the nearest huntable mob by uuid, greedy-walks to its moving cell, and swings on cooldown when in reach.

name type required default desc count int no 0 (until none) stop after N kills (0/omit = until none) targets string no cfg.hunt.targets override huntable ids — JSON array ["minecraft:cow"] or CSV

Phases: SEEK → CHASE → STRIKE (STRIKE → CHASE when the target moves out of reach, → SEEK when killed/lost). movementPhases: {CHASE}.

Completion: isDone when kills ≥ count (count > 0), or SEEK finds nothing after a grace window (cfg.hunt.seekGraceTicks) — never ERROR. Outputs: { kills }. onAbort: greedy release + release keys + nav stop.

Notable: the mob feed is a render-thread snapshot (world.mobs()) bridged main→worker; STRIKE is a crosshair attack(uuid) aimed by lookAt (no live entity ref off-thread), and a kill is confirmed only by the target vanishing next tick. Best-effort sword auto-equip (fists work). No explicit LOOT phase — a kill-spot linger lets vanilla auto-pickup grab the drops. SEEK tolerates transient empty snapshots (publish cadence race) before declaring done.

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "hunt", "params": {"count": 5, "targets": ["minecraft:cow"]}}'

docs.title: follow
docs.text:
Trail a peer at a follow-gap so the bot walks WITH them rather than shoving into them. It uses the fleet peer sensor. Persistent — runs until halted.

name type required default desc target string no null (nearest) peer username to follow (e.g. Steve); omit = nearest player/bot gap int no cfg.follow.gap hold this many blocks back

Phases: single FOLLOW phase. movementPhases: {FOLLOW}.

Completion: isDone always false — only halt/stop/abort ends it. Losing the peer stands and re-acquires (by uuid, falling back to name/nearest), it does not end the mission. Outputs: { target }. onAbort: greedy release + release keys + nav stop.

Notable: the target feed is the render-thread peer snapshot (world.peers()) bridged main→worker. Hysteresis (a comfort band around gap) prevents walk/stop stutter when the leader stands still. A custom progress policy exempts the stall watchdog whenever the bot is holding/waiting (a deliberate hold ≠ a wedge) and only watches feet while actively driving. Never ERRORs.

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "follow", "params": {"target": "Steve", "gap": 3}}'

docs.title: interact
docs.text:
Right-click a held item onto a target block or item-frame entity — the mission-shaped counterpart of the storage drawer's look-aimed use and the interact_place ext primitive.

name type required default desc x int yes — target block X y int yes — target block Y z int yes — target block Z item string no keep held item id to hold + place face string no toward the bot face to right-click profile string no (resolved) target kind: frame | display | generic verify string no (profile default) override verify: consumed | none

Phases: GOTO → INTERACT → IDLE (INTERACT is an internal AIM → USE → VERIFY). movementPhases: {GOTO}.

Completion: isDone on a successful VERIFY (INTERACT_DONE) or any give-up (INTERACT_GAVE_UP). Outputs: { placed }. onAbort: nav stop.

Notable: the frame profile targets a vanilla item-frame entity (not a block): AIM resolves the nearest frame uuid via world.frames() (the mc_frames bridge) and USE calls useOnEntity — no frame found → fail loud (never a silent block click). display/generic go through useOnBlock. AIM/USE straddle a tick boundary (rotation must flush first); VERIFY waits cfg.interact.graceTicks (server-authoritative). GOTO has a blocked-but-in-reach fallback — if already within cfg.interact.reach, it interacts anyway.

./gerda ctl send mission_start '{"name": "interact", "params": {"x": 100, "y": 65, "z": 200, "item": "minecraft:diamond", "profile": "frame"}}'

docs.title: Mission chaining
docs.text:
The kernel consults exactly one MissionSequencer (src/shared/kernel/sequencer.ts) when a mission completes (isDone → true). The default IDLE_SEQUENCER collapses to IDLE; the orchestrator (src/bot/orchestrator/, an always-on capability wired in worker-bundle.ts) installs its own sequencer to run plans — ordered lists of mission steps. It drives kernel.startMission/abortMission for everything, preserving the single-active-mission invariant (it is not itself a mission).

A plan step names a mission plus optional params, guards, drive mode and control flow (loop, retry, branch); the complete step shape is in EXTENDING.md § Writing a plan. Each step runs autonomously (mode: "auto") or waits for an operator command (proceed/run/step/select), gated on the step's guards (e.g. inventoryHasRoom(0.9)). A typo'd mission name parks the plan in failed.

Outputs feed the next step's params. A step's params may be a static object OR a ParamBinding — (prev) => params, where prev is the just-completed mission's outputs(ctx) (captured before teardown). This is how mine's { mined, origin } or prospect's { target } can bind into the following step.

Registered plans (built in worker-bundle.ts): gather-and-mine (chop → mine), sustain-mine-smelt, and the dynamic sustain-cycle (mine → return → collect → load → craft → store → prospect, looping via next: () => 0). Drive plans with:

./gerda ctl send plan_start '{"name": "gather-and-mine"}'
./gerda ctl send run          # flip to auto, drain to completion
./gerda ctl send plan_status  # cursor + blocked reason + active mission
./gerda ctl send plans        # the registered plan names

plan_status replies with result.data = {plan, cursor, status, blockedReason, currentStep, activeMission, phase}, and logs the same fields as ORCH_STATUS.

See docs/EXTENDING.md for authoring plans and the guard/ParamBinding API.

docs.title: Test your mod in a real game
docs.text:
You write a Minecraft mod or maintain a modpack, and you want to check its behaviour in a running game: a block drops only for the right tool, a recipe exists, a machine reacts. Unit tests do not start Minecraft, and checking by hand does not repeat. This page shows how to run such checks with the Gerda harness, headless, in a container, from a few commands.

What you get:

  • A real Minecraft client with your mod, in a rootless podman container. It needs no GPU and no screen: the game renders in software on a virtual display.
  • A bridge into the running client. Through it you read the world, the player and the screens, send chat and commands, take screenshots, and run JavaScript with full Java access (jeval), so you can call your mod's own classes.
  • Arenas: test files that build a small scene and then assert game state. An assertion that does not hold fails the run with the value it got.
  • A video of the run, recorded off the virtual display and checked to be not black.

The worked example below tests a feature of GregTech CEu, the mod at the center of the Monifactory pack: tungstate ore drops only for an iron pickaxe or better.

docs.title: 1. Get the repo and the sandbox
docs.text:
You need Linux with rootless podman and internet access. Clone the repo:

git clone https://github.com/flamerix-ai/gerda
cd gerda

The sandbox lives in scripts/sandbox/. Its README has the requirements (RAM, disk, CPU), every step, the measured times and why each part is built the way it is: scripts/sandbox/README.md. Build the image and start the container:

scripts/sandbox/provision.sh build      # the image (Ubuntu 24.04, Java 21, Xvfb, Mesa, ffmpeg)
scripts/sandbox/provision.sh up         # the container

The repo step clones the harness into the container. Its place in the order matters: matrix and pack need it to run first, and the Monifactory client gets the harness only from a repo that runs after client. Sections 2 and 4 show the order.

provision.sh shell opens a shell in the container. After repo, the clone is ~/gerda there. In this page, provision.sh … lines run on your machine, and every other command runs in that shell, in ~/gerda.

docs.title: 2. Put your mod into a game
docs.text: Pick one of two paths.

docs.title: Path A: your mod in a vanilla + loader instance
docs.text:
matrix builds four instances (vanilla + loader + jsMacros), each with a single-player world called New World, generated in peaceful mode with cheats allowed (the arena commands need them):

scripts/sandbox/provision.sh repo https://github.com/flamerix-ai/gerda   # the harness, inside
scripts/sandbox/provision.sh matrix
scripts/sandbox/provision.sh add-mods Fabric-1.20.1 path/to/yourmod.jar
scripts/sandbox/provision.sh start-matrix Fabric-1.20.1           # opens New World, waits for the bridge
Instance Loader Bridge port Fabric-1.20.1 Fabric loader + Fabric API 55560 Fabric-1.21 Fabric loader + Fabric API 55561 Forge-1.18.2 Forge 40.3.0 55562 Vanilla-Forge-1.20.1 Forge 47.4.13 55563

matrix prints the ports, and ~/matrix/mc-bots.json keeps them. Check that the game loaded your mod:

P=55560
./gerda ctl --port $P ping
./gerda ctl --port $P send jeval '{"code":"Java.type(\"net.fabricmc.loader.api.FabricLoader\").getInstance().isModLoaded(\"yourmodid\")"}'

On Forge, ask Java.type("net.minecraftforge.fml.ModList").get().isLoaded("yourmodid") instead.

docs.title: Path B: your modpack
docs.text:
pack builds a test instance from a CurseForge-format modpack zip (manifest.json + overrides/). It gives the zip to the launcher's own import, as a player does: the launcher downloads the mods with its own CurseForge access. Then pack adds jsMacros when a pinned build matches and generates a world:

scripts/sandbox/provision.sh repo https://github.com/flamerix-ai/gerda   # skip if done for path A
scripts/sandbox/provision.sh pack MyPack path/to/MyPack.zip
scripts/sandbox/provision.sh start-matrix MyPack

A zip given by URL needs its sha256 as the third argument, or --unpinned to take it unchecked (then it is downloaded again on every run). The step writes the folder, name and sha256 of each installed mod file to ~/.sbx/pack-MyPack-files.tsv. Nothing pins these files.

If the import cannot finish by itself, install the pack once in your own launcher. Then give the step that instance's folder with --from. The step takes the mod files from that folder:

scripts/sandbox/provision.sh pack MyPack path/to/MyPack.zip --from ~/.local/share/PrismLauncher/instances/MyPack

The import cannot finish by itself when a mod author keeps a file out of third-party launchers and no copy of the file is on Modrinth. The step then fails and names each blocked file with its CurseForge page. Section 7 tells more.

The reference pack is set up by its own steps, with a dedicated server: server, client, repo and start install and run Monifactory 0.13.4 with the bot account joined on bridge port 55544. The worked example in section 4 runs there.

docs.title: 3. Write a test: an arena
docs.text:
An arena is a JSON file in scenarios/arenas/. Its file name is its name. ops build the scene with operator commands, then each entry of checks runs one jeval and compares the JSON value it returns with expect:

{
  "desc": "my block needs a diamond pickaxe",
  "ops": [
    { "op": "clear", "from": [-2, 101, -2], "to": [2, 104, 3] },
    { "op": "fill",  "from": [-2, 100, -2], "to": [2, 100, 3], "block": "minecraft:stone" },
    { "op": "set",   "pos": [0, 101, 2], "block": "mymod:my_block" },
    { "op": "clearinv" },
    { "op": "give",  "item": "minecraft:diamond_pickaxe" },
    { "op": "player", "pos": [0, 101, 0] },
    { "op": "wait",  "ticks": 40 }
  ],
  "checks": [
    {
      "desc": "the block is there",
      "jeval": "World.getBlock(0, 101, 2).getId()",
      "expect": "mymod:my_block"
    },
    {
      "desc": "it drops only for the correct tool",
      "jeval": "World.getBlock(0, 101, 2).getBlockStateHelper().isToolRequired()",
      "expect": true
    }
  ]
}
  • ops (all of them: scripts/dev/arena.py, top of the file): clear and fill a box, set one block, clearinv, give an item, select a hotbar slot, player teleports the client, wait sleeps a number of ticks. The wait at the end gives the server time to sync the blocks and items back to the client before the checks read them.
  • jeval code is JavaScript with the full jsMacros and Java scope: World, Player, Client, Java.type(...) for any class, your mod's included. The value of the last expression is the result. expect is compared as canonical JSON, so true is not 1.
  • Every check runs, also after one fails. The arena passes only when all of them pass.
  • An arena can also run a bot mission and assert its log events (mission + expect.events); that is how the Gerda bot's own behaviour is tested (TESTING.md).

docs.title: Make the test able to fail: a known-bad twin
docs.text:
A check that cannot fail proves nothing. Pair each arena with a known-bad twin: the same file with a known_bad key that says what it wrongly claims, and "wrong": true on each check whose expect is wrong on purpose. Each marked check needs exactly one unmarked check in the same file with the same jeval and the right value as its expect; the arena does not load without it. A marked check passes only when its own answer is exactly that right value and the unmarked check passed too: the game refused the wrong claim by giving the right answer. The other checks keep their correct values and must pass as usual.

So the known-bad fails when the game accepts the wrong value, because then the check cannot tell right from wrong. It also fails on any other answer: a jeval error, a null, a third value (for example, the pickaxe was never given), or when a scene check fails (the block was not placed). A broken setup never counts as a pass.

docs.title: 4. Worked example: GregTech CEu ore needs the right pickaxe
docs.text:
gtceu-ore-harvest-tier.json places gtceu:tungstate_ore, gives the player a stone pickaxe (hotbar slot 0) and an iron pickaxe (slot 1), and asks the game's own harvest predicate with each one in hand. Player.hasCorrectToolForDrops is the method Forge calls when a block breaks, to decide if it drops anything. The check selects the slot and returns both the held item and the answer:

(function () {
  Player.openInventory().setSelectedHotbarSlotIndex(0);   // the stone pickaxe
  var p = Player.getPlayer();
  var state = World.getBlock(0, 101, 2).getBlockStateHelper().getRaw();
  return { held: p.getMainHand().getItemId(),
           drops: p.getRaw()[srg('Player', 'hasCorrectToolForDrops')](state) };
})()

getRaw() gives the Minecraft object. On Forge its methods have SRG names (m_36298_); srg(class, member) looks the name up for you (EXTENDING.md § SRG-mapping workflow). Its twin, gtceu-ore-harvest-tier-knownbad.json, keeps the ore check and the stone-pickaxe check as they are, and adds the same stone-pickaxe question once more, marked "wrong": true, claiming that the stone pickaxe gets the drop.

Run it in the Monifactory sandbox. The arena ops are operator commands, and the bot plays as a normal non-op player, so give it operator rights from the server console for the test, and take them back after:

scripts/sandbox/provision.sh server && scripts/sandbox/provision.sh client
scripts/sandbox/provision.sh repo https://github.com/flamerix-ai/gerda   # again if it ran before client
scripts/sandbox/provision.sh start && scripts/sandbox/provision.sh verify
scripts/sandbox/provision.sh console op student_bot

In the container shell:

just gate-live gtceu-ore-harvest-tier gtceu-ore-harvest-tier-knownbad

The output. The values are the ones a run in a fresh sandbox returned:

── gtceu-ore-harvest-tier ──
  8 ops applied
  [PASS] the placed block is GTCEu tungstate ore: "gtceu:tungstate_ore"
  [PASS] it drops only for the correct tool: true
  [PASS] a stone pickaxe in hand gets no drop: {"held": "minecraft:stone_pickaxe", "drops": false}
  [PASS] an iron pickaxe in hand gets the drop: {"held": "minecraft:iron_pickaxe", "drops": true}
  [PASS] checks
── gtceu-ore-harvest-tier-knownbad ──
  8 ops applied
  [PASS] the placed block is GTCEu tungstate ore: "gtceu:tungstate_ore"
  [PASS] a stone pickaxe in hand gets no drop: {"held": "minecraft:stone_pickaxe", "drops": false}
  [PASS] WRONG ON PURPOSE: a stone pickaxe in hand gets the drop: refused the wrong {"held": "minecraft:stone_pickaxe", "drops": true} — got the right {"held": "minecraft:stone_pickaxe", "drops": false}
  [PASS] checks
=== gate summary ===
  PASS  gtceu-ore-harvest-tier
  PASS  gtceu-ore-harvest-tier-knownbad
[gate] 2/2 passed

A failing check prints got …, expected …, and the command exits 1. Exit 2 means there was no verdict: no client answered on the bridge. After the test:

scripts/sandbox/provision.sh console deop student_bot

just gate-live with no names runs every arena in scenarios/arenas/, including the bot's own. Name yours to run only them.

On a test-root instance (path A or B) the player is the world's owner, so it needs no op. Run an arena against its port with the arena tool:

python3 scripts/dev/arena.py run my-block-check --port 55560
python3 scripts/dev/arena.py clean my-block-check --port 55560   # the scene back to air

arena.py run exits 0 on a pass and 1 on a fail, like the gate; it does not clean up.

docs.title: 5. Screenshots and video
docs.text:
Screenshots come from the game itself:

./gerda ctl send screenshot     # writes <instance>/minecraft/screenshots/ai_shot.png

provision.sh fetch <path> copies a file out of the container. A path without a leading / is relative to the container user's home.

To record a video, run record while the test runs, for example from a second terminal:

scripts/sandbox/provision.sh record 60 gtceu-run.mp4

record films the window of the running client with ffmpeg (x11grab on the virtual display, h264, 30 fps) and measures the file with scripts/rig/motion_probe.py: the mean brightness (luma) of the sampled frames, and how much the picture moves. A recording whose mean luma is under 30 of 255 fails as black. A good one is copied to your machine. Add --detach to record in the background; provision.sh wait record then waits for it, and provision.sh fetch recordings/<name>.mp4 copies it out.

The video runs at the speed of the game. Software rendering gives about 20-30 fps.

docs.title: 6. Drive it from an LLM
docs.text:
The MCP server (mcp/server.py) gives an LLM client the same bridge as tools: mc_ping, mc_get_state, mc_send (any bridge command, jeval too) and the fleet tools. mc://api lists every command. The server runs inside the container and talks MCP over stdio, so a client on your machine can start it through podman exec:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mc": {
      "command": "podman",
      "args": ["exec", "-i", "-u", "student", "-w", "/home/student/gerda", "gerda-sandbox",
               "uv", "run", "mcp/server.py"]
    }
  }
}

Set MC_BRIDGE_PORT (for example with "env" in that entry, or podman exec -e) to talk to a test-root instance instead of 55544. From Python scripts, mcp/bridge_client.py is the client: BridgeClient(host="127.0.0.1", port=P).send("jeval", {"code": "..."}).

docs.title: 7. Limits
docs.text:
• Speed. Software rendering is slow: the modded client takes several minutes to load, and right after a join the bridge answers late for a minute. Retry the first command. A check that depends on timing can fail on a busy machine.
  • Offline accounts. The sandbox plays with offline accounts (online-mode=false). There is no Microsoft login, so no Realms and no online-mode servers.
  • Forge vs Fabric. The harness (bridge, screenshots, jeval, arenas, MCP) works on every Minecraft version that has a jsMacros build. srg() and the SRG names are Forge-only: on Fabric, raw Minecraft methods have intermediary names (method_…), so prefer the jsMacros helpers there. The Gerda bot moves only on Forge. See PORTABILITY.md.
  • jsMacros sets the version range. No jsMacros build for your Minecraft version means no harness. Which versions have one: PORTABILITY.md.
  • CurseForge downloads. The sandbox does not download from CurseForge itself. pack and the Monifactory client step give the modpack zip to the launcher's own import (FreesmLauncher, a Prism Launcher fork). The launcher gets the files through its own access to the official CurseForge API, so it keeps the choice of each mod author:
  • A file that its author keeps out of third-party launchers comes from the author's own Modrinth upload, when there is one. In Monifactory 0.13.4, one file comes this way (entityculling), and it is the same file, byte for byte.
  • Otherwise the launcher asks for a manual download. The sandbox does not wait for a click. The step fails and prints each blocked file with its CurseForge page.

The fallback for either step is --from <folder>: install the pack once in your own launcher (blocked files downloaded by hand), then point the step at that instance's folder. The step copies the mod files from there. For Monifactory, the step checks every file against the sha256 pins (monifactory-0.13.4-client-files.tsv), the same check as after the import. A missing or changed file fails. For a pack of your own, the step records the files and their sha256, and nothing pins them. - Client-side view. jeval runs in the client. It reads the client's copy of the world, which the server keeps in sync, and calls game logic on the client side. Logic that only the server runs (a machine's recipe processing, world generation) is not directly reachable from a multiplayer client; in a single-player world the integrated server is in the same process. - Not tested here: NeoForge and Quilt instances, more than one test-root client at a time, and hosts other than Linux with rootless podman.

docs.title: Works on your Minecraft version
docs.text:
You play a different Minecraft version, or no modpack at all? This page says, honestly, what runs where today, and gives a short recipe to try it on a plain vanilla instance. The rest of the docs assume our reference setup: Monifactory 0.13.x on Forge 1.20.1 with jsMacros 1.9.2.

Gerda is two things, and they port differently:

  • The harness (harness/ — bridge, main, ext, eyes & hands, ./gerda ctl, the MCP server) talks to the game through jsMacros' own API and plain Java. It runs on every Minecraft version that has a jsMacros build, Forge or Fabric. Your own plain-JS bot (BUILD_YOUR_OWN_BOT.md) uses the same API, so it runs there too.
  • Gerda Bot (the src/ bundle — missions, navigator, reflexes) also calls raw Minecraft methods by their Forge SRG names (m_146922_ and friends). It moves on Forge. On Fabric those names do not exist: the bot loads, but refuses to move (see below).

docs.text:
Tested with the versions in each row, in a clean Ubuntu 24.04 container, single-player world, no modpack unless the row says so. "Measured" cells were run live, the Fabric and 1.18.2 bot cells in a re-test of the portability fixes.

The first gate is jsMacros itself: no jsMacros build for your version, no harness and no bot. Builds that exist (Modrinth jsmacros project, up to 1.9.3-beta; the newest is a 2024 beta, nothing for 1.21.2+):

docs.title: What "not supported" looks like, so you recognise it
docs.text:
On a Fabric (or any non-SRG) runtime the harness tells you itself:

  • ./gerda ctl diag → main.srgCheck.ok is "0" and srgCheck.runtime.reason says Fabric/intermediary runtime (Minecraft class is net.minecraft.class_310). The one boot log line for the check starts with !!! SRG boot-check FAIL.
  • The SRG-based GUI hands — click {x,y}, scroll, type, keypress — answer an error naming the missing SRG method. key, read_screen, close_screen and the widget clicks click {i} / click {text} use jsMacros' own API and keep working.
  • A movement mission (goto, mine, drill, …) releases every key on its first step and goes to ERROR; the journal (./gerda ctl get_logs) has MISSION_FATAL with RUNTIME_UNSUPPORTED: player.onGround failed (…) — or interact.setYaw failed, whichever SRG call the drive makes first (measured: player.onGround). The bot never walks without a heading: before this check, goto on Fabric walked straight along yaw 0 and fell 19 blocks.
  • ./gerda smoke fails two checks, player.onGround and interact.setYaw(current) (the navigator's steer path), even though interact.lookAt passes: 19/21.

Everywhere, on every version without those mods: emi_*, prospect, drill, and the quest tools fail with a "class not found" error naming the class (prospect says prospect needs GregTech CEu: …). Nothing else is affected.

If the bot bundle does not load at all, every bot command answers no module loaded, and ./gerda ctl get_state shows why under worker.fatal (worker.status is load_failed).

docs.title: Easy recipe — a vanilla instance on any version in the matrix
docs.text:
1. Launcher. Install a MultiMC-family launcher — FreesmLauncher or Prism Launcher — and add an offline account (SETUP.md step 3, items 1–2). The launcher picks the right Java for the version by itself (1.21 needs Java 21).
  2. Instance. Add Instance → Vanilla → your version, and under Mod loader pick Forge (or Fabric if you only want the harness). Use a name without spaces, for example Forge-1.20.1. Fabric API is not needed by jsMacros.
  3. jsMacros. Download the ONE jar for your version and loader from https://modrinth.com/mod/jsmacros/versions into the instance's minecraft/mods/ folder (launcher: right-click the instance → Folder). The JavaScript engine is inside that jar; there is nothing else to install.
  4. World and first starts. Start the instance, Singleplayer → Create New World (Peaceful is easiest), then Save and Quit and close the game. Start it once more and close it again: the second start upgrades config/jsMacros/options.json to "version": 3, and services registered before that upgrade are lost.
  5. Deploy. From the repo: just sync (point it at your launcher first if needed — SETUP.md step 3, item 4). It writes into every instance that has jsMacros and gives each its own bridge port in <instance>/minecraft/config/jsMacros/Macros/bridge_port.txt (the first one gets 55544). If another client is running, add --skip <thatInstance>.
  6. Register the services (game closed): add main and bridge to core.services in options.json, or use the in-game jsMacros GUI (default key J) → Services → +. Both ways: SETUP.md step 6.
  7. Check. Start the game and open your world, then ./gerda ctl --port <port> --wait-ready 60 ping → pong, and ./gerda ctl --port <port> get_state shows your position. The MCP server works the same way with MC_BRIDGE_HOST=127.0.0.1 MC_BRIDGE_PORT=<port>. ./gerda ctl --port <port> diag shows srgCheck: "1" on Forge, "0" with a reason on Fabric.
  8. Walk (Forge only). ./gerda ctl --port <port> send mission_start '{"name": "goto", "params": {"x": 100, "y": 64, "z": 200}}'. (./gerda ctl goto is a Baritone chat command, not our navigator.)

Version-specific notes. Before 1.20 there is no quick-play: open the world from Singleplayer → Play Selected World yourself. The SRG names the bot uses are the same on Forge 1.18.2 and 1.20.1, so the 1.20.1 harness/srg_names.json is fine there; ./gerda srg itself reads 1.20.1 Forge mappings by default and needs --proguard / --merged paths for anything else (./gerda srg -h).

docs.title: Your own bot on any version — the portable path
docs.text:
The plain-JS template uses only jsMacros' API, so it runs everywhere the harness runs (measured on Forge 1.20.1, Forge 1.18.2, Fabric 1.20.1 and Fabric 1.21):

  1. Copy harness/bot_template.js to yourbot.js; keep its last line, globalThis.Module = MyModule;.
  2. Deploy it as the worker bundle into that one instance: ./gerda sync -s yourbot.js -n __gerda_bot.bundle.js --only <instance>, then ./gerda ctl --port <port> send reload_worker.
  3. Every command the container does not own reaches your command(): ./gerda ctl --port <port> send my_start.

Details: BUILD_YOUR_OWN_BOT.md.

docs.title: Another modpack on Forge 1.20.1
docs.text:
Everything version-bound stays valid; only the content changes.

Layer Depends on Portability Kernel, FSM, capabilities, reflexes the Runtime facade Pack-agnostic. Loads on any jsMacros runtime (no host class is looked up while the bundle loads); the facade calls that need Forge SRG report their failure as a typed error. Navigator (src/shared/nav/) block ids + the SRG steer/ground calls Pack-agnostic, Forge-only (see the matrix). Missions mine, goto, chop, hunt, fetch, stash, search, follow, loot-run, storage, craft, smelt, interact vanilla mechanics Pack-agnostic. mine targets the ore table below. Without Functional Storage, deposit routing uses chests only. Ore set + harvest tiers (config/ores_live.json) the pack's Forge registry Regenerated from any pack: just extract-ores-live reads the live registry (forge:ores tag + *_ore ids + needs_*_tool tags) through a running bot. Missions drill and prospect GTCEu HV prospector GregTech only. Elsewhere, use the mine mission on the regenerated ore table. ext.js plugins prospect, emi_search/emi_recipe/emi_uses, quest tools GTCEu / EMI / FTB Quests Optional. Each handler resolves its mod classes when called; without the mod, that one command fails loudly. Quest autopilot (scripts/objective/) FTB Quests (adapter) Optional. The engine is mod-agnostic; adapters live in scripts/objective/sources/. Raw-Java calls in the harness and the bundle Forge SRG names The version and loader boundary — next section.

Recipe: install jsMacros, just sync, register the services (SETUP.md); with a bot in the world run just extract-ores-live, then just build && just sync; verify with ./gerda smoke and a few arenas (./gerda gate) on an opped test bot. A plain Forge 1.20.1 instance with no modpack needs no ore regeneration at all: the vanilla ores are already in the table.

docs.title: Porting the bot to Fabric or NeoForge (contributors)
docs.text:
The bundle loads and fails loud on these runtimes, so a port is now a bounded job:

  1. A runtime name table. The 17 hardcoded SRG tokens live in two tables, each entry commented with its Mojang signature: 7 in harness/main.js (screen input + the sprint applier), mirrored as HARNESS_SCREEN_SRG in src/core/runtime/jsmacros/srg.ts, and 10 in the SRG table of the same file. Fabric needs the intermediary names (method_… / field_…); NeoForge 1.20.5+ runs on the Mojang names. Select the table at boot from the runtime check that diag already reports (srgCheck.runtime, src/shared/harness/srg-runtime.ts).
  2. A mapping source for scripts/dev/srg.py for that loader (today it reads Forge mappings), so srg(), reflect and the boot self-check work there too.
  3. Re-check movement constants. Sprint-jump distances and water-clutch timing (src/shared/config/schema.ts, movement and physics sections) are tuned on 1.20.1; run the nav arenas (scenarios/arenas/) to catch drift.
  4. Verify with ./gerda smoke (all checks, including interact.setYaw(current)) and a goto mission that arrives.

Other contributions with the seams already in place:

  • A pack profile = a regenerated config/ores_live.json, plus notes on which optional plugins apply. No code.
  • A non-GT vein strategy for drill = another source of vein targets for the same mission. See MISSIONS.md and src/bot/missions/drill/.
  • A quest adapter = a new ObjectiveSource in scripts/objective/sources/, next to ftb_quests.py and local_goals.py.

Open an issue or a Discussion with your pack and version before you start, and read CONTRIBUTING.md for the gates.

docs.title: RIG.md — booting bot clients off-screen: filming and headless running
docs.text:
Two flows over one boot script, scripts/ops/capture_rig.sh:

  • Film — record the bot doing real work (mine → smelt → restock), hands-free.
  • Run — boot one bot client invisibly and drive it over the bridge. No camera.

Both start Minecraft inside an independent headless sway compositor (output HEADLESS-1). Nothing appears on your monitor or steals focus. The script's header explains the capture model. Two agent skills in Claude Code format, /gerda-film and /gerda-run (.claude/skills/), follow this doc.

Tested on: Linux, NVIDIA GPU (proprietary driver), sway headless (wlroots) + Xwayland, wf-recorder, ffmpeg, FreesmLauncher, Nix. It has run live only on the maintainer's machine. Automated checks cover build and just check in a clean container; none boots a client.

docs.title: Shared topology
docs.text:
role instance account bridge notes worker Monifactory_bot_1 bot_1 55545 non-op, runs the bundle camera Monifactory_bot_2 your op account 55546 op spectator: camera and item source camera + shader (optional) a copy of the camera instance your op account the camera's port replaces the camera; never boot both

Examples assume the default assignment (worker 55545, camera 55546); substitute the ports mc-bots.json gave your instances.

  • Ports come from the machine-local mc-bots.json (gitignored); just sync keeps an instance's existing port. Verify after every sync: the file is <instanceDir>/minecraft/config/jsMacros/Macros/bridge_port.txt, a mc_bridge_port GlobalVar overrides it, and on a running client python3 scripts/ops/bridge_ctl.py --port <port> bridge_diag reports the live value (it answers even when main is deaf). Machine state files (mc-bots.json, mc-tasks.json, local.config.json) resolve from git rev-parse --git-common-dir (scripts/machine_root.py), so every worktree shares one registry; --separate-git-dir clones are unsupported.
  • Names come from local.config.json (copy the .example; env vars win): cameraAccountName / MC_CAMERA_ACCOUNT_NAME is the op camera account (python3 scripts/local_config.py camera_account_name); serverRoot / MC_SERVER_ROOT locates the server (python3 scripts/local_config.py server_dir, see SERVER_SETUP.md). The demo scripts refuse to run without them.
  • Server: "$(python3 scripts/local_config.py server_ctl)" {start|status|cmd "<console>"|log} — always day, peaceful, offline mode, localhost:25565. The console has full op authority.
  • The bot plays like a real player: no cheats; its only server privilege is teleport. What the filmed scenes hand it and reset around it is listed in What the filmed scenes stage.
  • Devshell: boot and record commands run under nix develop .#capture -c … (sway, Xwayland, wf-recorder, ffmpeg, grim, fontconfig, python3). freesmlauncher must be on PATH. Bridge driving is plain python3.
  • Boot serially. Two modded clients booting at once deadlock mod loading. Worker first, wait for its bridge, then the camera.
  • Co-launch guard. A same-name login kicks whoever holds the account, so capture_rig.sh refuses to launch while another launcher client runs. Booting the camera over your own worker needs ALLOW_CONCURRENT=1.

docs.title: What the filmed scenes stage
docs.text:
The filmed scenes are staged. Scripts, the server console and the op camera build each scene, supply the bot and reset the scene between laps. Once a mission or plan runs, the bot's moves are its own.

No /give targets the bot. Every item it is handed goes the same way: the server console gives it to the op camera account, the camera drops it, and the bot picks it up.

  • Sets. The server console builds the sustain-loop stage (sustain_live.py build). The other sets were built live (console fills) and later captured as data; arena.py build restages them (see § Sets below).
  • Position. The shot list's console lines teleport the bot into place for 01_clutch, 02a_prospect and 05_economy (scenarios/shots/teaser.json).
  • Stage seal (sustain loop). sustain_live.py build also makes the stage floor bedrock and lays a ring of invisible barrier blocks around it, so the bot cannot dig a pit or walk off, and it empties the bot's cached prospect veins so that the plan does not walk to a far vein. sustain_live.py storage places the deposit chest and registers it with the bot (storage_add).
  • Starter kit (sustain loop). The camera gets 32 coal, 32 cobblestone and 1 crafting table and drops them; a console tp @e[type=item] moves the dropped items onto the bot (sustain_live.py supply). Film staging only — fleet play never hands the bot items (see FLEET_PLAYBOOK § 1).
  • Pickaxe (sustain loop). The bot's diamond pickaxe came the same way, as a manual step before filming; no script does it. The plan crafts only the spare (src/bot/plans/sustain-cycle.ts).
  • Between laps (sustain loop). Each lap (driven by sustain_live.py loop) aborts the plan, replaces the three furnaces with empty ones, refills the 25-block iron-ore patch, teleports the bot back to (3, 101, 1) and fills the two outer furnaces with console data so that they glow. The bot loads only the centre furnace. Each lap ends by restarting the plan; loop waits LAP_DWELL_S seconds after each lap.
  • Vein shot (03_vein). The bot mines a built room lined with iron ore and lit by invisible light blocks (set 03_ore_chamber).
  • Shaft shot (02b_shaft). The vein is chosen in advance; for the filmed take the marker was edited by hand. On a restage, the marker op of set 03_ore_chamber writes an iron vein on column (-343, -70) into the world store of the instance in MC_INST (the bot's instance, see § Sets), so drill sinks its shaft there, through natural rock into the ore room.
  • Clutch shot (01_clutch). The water bucket came the same way, as a manual step; the shot list notes it, and no script runs it. scripts/demo/walk_off.sh presses the forward key for 500 ms to step the bot off the ledge. The water placement and the scoop back are the bot's reflex.

The teaser caption "Every block earned — no /give, no cheats" describes the bot: no /give targets it, and it runs no cheat command. "Every block earned" is not literal: the kit's cobblestone and crafting table were dropped to the bot, and the console places and refills the ore it mines in the sustain loop. The scene around the bot is staged as listed here.

docs.title: capture_rig.sh flags
docs.text:
-a account  -l instance   FreesmLauncher profile + instance dir (required)
-s host:port              join a server after boot (else title screen)
-R WxH                    headless resolution (default 1920x1080, always @60Hz)
-c codec                  encoder (default libx264; h264_nvenc only once NVENC works on your driver)
-o out.mp4  -t seconds    record file / duration (0 = until client exit or Ctrl-C)
-H "cmd"                  READY hook, run once before recording
-K                        boot and keep alive; do not record
-P                        use the capture options profile; restore the playing one on exit

-P swaps options.txt for the recording profile: no view bob, no FOV pulse, no screen warp, gamma 1.0, FOV about 90, render distance 16, enableVsync:false. Use it on the camera for every take. A failed swap is fatal. scripts/rig/teardown.sh also restores the profile, so a client killed from outside does not stay on it.

The -H hook gets CAM_WAYLAND (the camera's sway display), CAM_SWAYSOCK, CAM_XDISPLAY, MC_INSTANCE and MC_LOG. A hook failure is a warning.

docs.title: 0. Deploy before the camera boots
docs.text:
A sync rewrites the service files in every instance; jsMacros restarts them, and the camera's per-frame Forge listener (from harness/ext.js) cannot be unregistered, so the camera crashes. Deploy first, boot the camera second. If the camera is already up:

./gerda sync --skip <camera-instance>     # or: just sync --skip <camera-instance>

--skip is repeatable, excludes the instance from bundle, services and bridge_port.txt, and errors on an unknown name. The worker tolerates a live sync.

docs.title: 1. Boot the worker and wait for its bridge
docs.text:
nix develop .#capture -c scripts/ops/capture_rig.sh \
  -a bot_1 -l Monifactory_bot_1 -s localhost:25565 -K &
python3 scripts/ops/bridge_ctl.py --port 55545 --wait-ready 90 status

--wait-ready retries until status answers. --wait only waits for the port to open (the bridge listens from the title screen but answers only in-world), and --timeout does not wait at all. For a guaranteed in-world state, check that get_state reports a position.

docs.title: 2. Stage the scene
docs.text:
scripts/demo/sustain_live.py builds the sustain-cycle arena through the server console:

python3 scripts/demo/sustain_live.py build     # floor + 25-block ore patch + 3 furnaces, sealed; clears prospect cache
python3 scripts/demo/sustain_live.py supply    # drop coal/cobble/table for the bot — needs the camera on 55546
python3 scripts/demo/sustain_live.py storage   # place + register the deposit chest — after supply

Order: build, boot the camera (step 3), then supply and storage (the step 3 hook runs them). supply acts through the op player on CAM_PORT (55546, or SHOOT_CAM_PORT); storage places the chest from the console and registers it over the bot's bridge. The sealed floor and barrier walls keep the bot in the arena; the cleared cache makes a mined-out patch return PROSPECT_EMPTY at once. loop re-arms the patch every 30 s.

docs.title: 3. Boot the camera with a READY hook
docs.text:
$RIG_TMP is any scratch dir (export RIG_TMP=$(mktemp -d)):

# $RIG_TMP/film_hook.sh
set -e
cd <repo>
python3 scripts/demo/sustain_live.py wait       # hook fires at the title menu: block until in-world
python3 scripts/demo/sustain_live.py supply     # kit drop — puts the camera in survival on the bot
python3 scripts/demo/sustain_live.py storage    # place + register the deposit chest
python3 scripts/demo/sustain_live.py frame      # LAST: camera pose + spectator + HUD off
WAYLAND_DISPLAY=$CAM_WAYLAND \
  ON_START="python3 scripts/demo/sustain_live.py loop 3 &" \
  scripts/rig/record.sh "$RIG_TMP/sustain_raw.mp4" 150 HEADLESS-1 60

ALLOW_CONCURRENT=1 nix develop .#capture -c scripts/ops/capture_rig.sh \
  -a "$(python3 scripts/local_config.py camera_account_name)" -l Monifactory_bot_2 -s localhost:25565 \
  -K -t 170 -H "bash $RIG_TMP/film_hook.sh"
  • Use -K. record.sh in the hook owns the recording; without -K a second recorder starts and its frame guard kills the keep-alive.
  • wait is the hook's first line. The hook runs before the camera's bridge listens; without it supply and frame get Connection refused.
  • frame runs after supply. supply switches the camera to survival and moves it onto the bot to drop the kit; frame puts it back in spectator at its pose. In the other order the take records from the bot's spawn cell.
  • record.sh runs wf-recorder with -D, so a static scene still records at a constant frame rate. If its frame guard fires anyway, the output is stuck: check swaymsg -t get_outputs (dead sway, wrong output name, mode not @60Hz).

docs.title: 4. Encode
docs.text:
nix develop .#capture -c scripts/rig/encode.sh "$RIG_TMP/sustain_raw.mp4" release/gerda_sustain_demo.mp4

h264, crf 20, preset slow, +faststart, no audio. A trailing 1440/1080/720 downscales. release/ is gitignored.

docs.title: 5. Verify and tear down
docs.text:
• ffprobe the encode and extract a few frames (ffmpeg -ss <t> -i out.mp4 -frames:v 1 f.png): bot mining, furnace lit, bot hauling to the chest.
  • Check motion with scripts/rig/motion_probe.py (§ Take acceptance).
  • scripts/rig/teardown.sh Monifactory_bot_1 Monifactory_bot_2 — kills the clients, leaves server and compositor up, restores any capture profile.

docs.title: Cinema commands (ext.js, camera bridge 55546)
docs.text:
command args effect cam_pose x,y,z,yaw?,pitch?,spectator? teleport the camera (/tp, optional /gamemode spectator) cam_aim yaw,pitch,roll?,smooth? set target angles; the per-frame hook eases toward them cam_look_at x,y,z,smooth? aim at a world point cam_free — release the hook cam_spectate target? /spectate <player>; no arg releases cam_hud hide? toggle Options.hideGui (F1) cam_state — mode, hooked, frame count, angles, last error

Scripted rotation is applied per tick and vanilla does not interpolate it, so the camera uses a Forge ViewportEvent.ComputeCameraAngles listener that eases angles every frame. From GraalJS, register with the explicit overload addListener(priority, receiveCancelled, EventClass, consumer) and wrap floats in Math.fround. Liveness: cam_state.frames climbs at about 60/s. 20/s means a tick fallback; 0 means the hook never registered (see cam_state.error).

docs.title: Shot runner
docs.text:
python3 scripts/demo/shoot.py list  scenarios/shots/teaser.json               # list shots
python3 scripts/demo/shoot.py pose  scenarios/shots/teaser.json 05_economy    # frame only
just shoot 05_economy                                                         # roll one or more ids
SHOTLIST=scenarios/shots/other.json just shoot 03_vein                        # another shot list

A shot declares camera pose, optional track (aim at the bot about 4×/s), console staging, bot command and duration. shoot.py poses, drives, records and writes <out_dir>/<id>.mp4. It boots nothing: bring up the worker and the camera (-K, camera with -P) first. A shot whose staging fails is skipped.

  • Roll with just shoot. It runs inside the capture devShell and finds the camera's display from the client on the camera port (SHOOT_CAM_PORT, default 55546). CAM_WAYLAND=wayland-N pins it (still verified). Every miss exits non-zero before staging.
  • A take counts only if ffprobe opens it and its duration is at least 0.8 × the shot's seconds (MIN_TAKE_RATIO). record.sh fails the take on any recorder error (135 = SIGBUS, 137 = SIGKILL). File size is never the verdict.
  • Open-world shots (teaser.json 01–04) have no camera coords. Fly the camera, screenshot, write the pose into the JSON, pose to confirm, then roll. Read the camera's screenshot from its own instance: MC_INST=<instances>/Monifactory_bot_2/minecraft python3 scripts/ops/mc_shot.py --file -s 0.4. Without MC_INST, mc_shot.py reads the human instance.

docs.title: Take acceptance
docs.text:
python3 scripts/rig/motion_probe.py take.mp4                                   # full frame
python3 scripts/rig/motion_probe.py take.mp4 --crop 780,420,360x360            # around the bot
python3 scripts/rig/motion_probe.py take.mp4 --in 20.6 --out 24.2              # only the used range
python3 scripts/rig/motion_probe.py take.mp4 --crop 780,420,360x360 --max-static 2.0   # as a gate
python3 scripts/rig/motion_probe.py 01_clutch.mp4 --in 3.2 --out 5.3 --preset static-hook
./gerda motion-probe take.mp4 --json

motion_probe.py measures the mean absolute difference (MAD) between neighbouring downsampled frames and prints live windows, static runs and the longest freeze. --max-static N gates on the longest freeze: exit 1 = fail, exit 2 = could not measure.

  • Run it twice: full frame (does the world move?) and --crop around the bot (does the bot move?). Crop coords are source pixels.
  • Read duty — the share of live samples. The gate sees only the longest freeze, so a take of short blinks passes it. Duty is reported, never gated.
  • Measure the used range with --in/--out; timestamps stay absolute. A range that is empty, inverted or not fully inside the file exits 2, and the message says whether the take is short or the container's start_time is offset (then subtract it or re-mux). The last ~0.2 s of a range (2/--fps) carries no measurement.
  • A short take plays fast. wf-recorder writes 60 fps timestamps, so a recorder that falls behind yields a shorter, sped-up file. The 0.8 duration floor is the only detector. A healthy take is 3.5–4 s longer than seconds.

Read duty relatively; there is no absolute floor. For reference, these values come from the maintainer's teaser takes: accepted segments of scenarios/shots/teaser_cut.json span 0–74 % (defaults, full frame), for example:

segment take in–out duty longest static economy_mine 05_economy 20.6–24.2 74.3 % 0.6 s climb 04_nav 0.6–5.8 56.9 % 0.1 s vein 03_vein 6.0–60.0 10.4 % 18.0 s hook_clutch 01_clutch 3.2–5.3 0.0 % 2.0 s

Static shots (in-pit camera, GUI insert, timelapse) read 0.0 % by design. Judge a take against a comparable reference — the same shot's good take, or its crop run. (A maintainer-only test pins these rows against the original footage; it skips without it.)

Driver log. A shot's during command logs to <out_dir>/<id>.during.log. sustain_live.py writes a plan witness per lap (STARTED / UNKNOWN_PLAN / no-evidence) and a mission_status line every 10 s, read from the worker journal <instances>/Monifactory_bot_1/minecraft/config/jsMacros/Macros/miner.ndjson (MC_WORKER_JOURNAL overrides). The probe says when the picture froze; the log says why.

docs.title: Static hook shots
docs.text:
A static hook is a still camera around one brief event: the 01_clutch water clutch, about 0.3 s of motion in the 3.2–5.3 cut. The defaults miss it. --preset static-hook uses measured values and gates on the event:

knob preset default why --thresh 0.3 1.0 well above dead-footage noise, well below the event's motion --min-live 0.2 s 0.5 s 2 samples; a brief event holds about 3 gate --min-windows 1 — on a still shot the question is "did the event happen" --fps / --scale / --bridge 10 / 192x108 / 0.5 same calibration values

The preset runs full frame; --crop is refused (exit 2). An explicit sensitivity flag overrides it with a WARN. On the maintainer's takes, the preset finds the clutch as one live window and fails both the clutch's dead tail and a parked-bot shot; the defaults find no window in any of them.

Limit: a single odd frame yields two MADs, which 0.2 s accepts; the threshold guards against it.

docs.title: GUI inserts
docs.text:
wf-recorder records an output, not a window. To film the bot's own GUI (02a_prospect), make the bot's window fullscreen on the shared output:

scripts/rig/fullscreen.sh --list                 # MC windows, instances, outputs
scripts/rig/fullscreen.sh Monifactory_bot_1      # bot's screen is recorded
scripts/rig/fullscreen.sh Monifactory_bot_2      # camera back

SWAYSOCK (or CAM_SWAYSOCK) pins one compositor. Needs the capture devShell.

docs.title: Shader camera instance (optional)
docs.text:
A shader camera is not required. To film with shaders:

  1. Copy the camera instance to a new instance. Name it Monifactory_cam_shader and ./gerda bind-accounts gives it the camera's account; under any other name, set the account yourself.
